Babadağ Mountain, Ölüdeniz, Fethiye, Turkey — the famous paragliding mountain

This is the takeoff ramp at around 1,700m - 1,900m. The main summit is 1,969m and it sits less than 5km from the sea, which is why it's one of the top paragliding sites in the world. 

What you are seeing is special:

The paved ramp you see with all the parachutes is the official launch. On this morning there is a low cloud inversion — a sea of clouds filling Fethiye Bay below you. The paragliders are launching _above_ the clouds and then floating over them at sunrise. In summer you usually see the turquoise Blue Lagoon below, but in winter / early morning you often get this break-up of the cloud cover from above.

In ancient times this mountain was known as Mount Cragus, a principal mountain of Lycia. It's limestone, covered with cedar and pine forests. The resort town of Fethiye stretches along the bay below it.
